title: Qatargate
subtitle: Cash-for-influence at the European Parliament

citizen.whatHappened: Politicians and people around the European Parliament were pulled into a Belgian corruption investigation over alleged secret payments from Qatar (and Morocco) meant to sway the Parliament. When police moved in, they found more than 1.5 million euros in cash. Several people were charged, and one former MEP admitted taking part. Years later, the case still has not reached a trial.

money.label: CASH SEIZED
money.note: Found by police during the investigation. A seizure is not a proven bribe, and no one has been convicted yet.

citizen.johnLine: John found 1.5 million euros before he found the paperwork.

executiveSummary: Qatargate is a cash-for-influence criminal investigation led by the Belgian Federal Prosecutor into allegations that Qatar and Morocco paid cash and gifts to members and staff of the European Parliament to influence Parliament's positions. It broke publicly on 9 December 2022 with police raids in Brussels, several arrests, and the seizure of more than 1.5 million euros in cash. As of the latest located procedural event, the case is still in the pre-trial (instruction) phase: no one has been tried or convicted by a court on the core charges. On 19-20 February 2026 the Brussels indictment chamber rejected the accused parties' attempts to annul the investigation and validated its continuation, a procedural decision that is expressly not a verdict on guilt. Every named living person denies wrongdoing except former MEP Pier Antonio Panzeri, who admitted participation under a January 2023 cooperation agreement.
whatIsAlleged: Prosecutors ALLEGE a corruption network in which Qatar and Morocco channelled cash and gifts to MEPs, former MEPs and NGO figures in exchange for favourable interventions inside the European Parliament, and that former MEP Pier Antonio Panzeri was the central organiser, partly through the Brussels NGO Fight Impunity. These remain allegations; no court has established them, and the individuals charged deny wrongdoing.
whatIsEstablished: Established as fact: more than 1.5 million euros in cash was physically seized during the December 2022 searches (a seizure, not a proven bribe). Pier Antonio Panzeri admitted criminal participation under a January 2023 cooperation agreement (an admission within that agreement, not a trial verdict). The European Parliament removed Eva Kaili as a Vice-President (13 December 2022) and later lifted the immunity of several MEPs. On 19-20 February 2026 the Brussels indictment chamber validated continuation of the procedure, stating this is in no way a definitive judgment on the legality or evidentiary value of the evidence. No conviction and no acquittal on the core charges has occurred. NO LATER PUBLIC PROCEDURAL UPDATE LOCATED AS OF 1 SEPTEMBER 2026.

title: Huaweigate
subtitle: Alleged cash-for-influence lobbying at the European Parliament

citizen.whatHappened: Belgian investigators suspect that lobbyists working for the tech company Huawei tried to influence people around the European Parliament using payments, gifts and football tickets. Police searched about 21 places, including Huawei's Brussels office, and charged eight people. Several MEPs were asked to give up their immunity so they could be investigated. Nothing has been proven in court, and the investigation is still running.

money.label: ALLEGED PAYMENTS
money.note: Figures come from leaked investigation material. Alleged, not proven, and the people named deny it.

citizen.johnLine: A letter warning about 'technological racism' that somehow forgot to mention the technology company.

executiveSummary: Huaweigate is a Belgian criminal investigation into alleged bribery of members and staff of the European Parliament by lobbyists working for the Chinese technology company Huawei. It became public on 13 March 2025, when Belgian federal police carried out about 21 searches across Belgium and Portugal, including Huawei's Brussels office, on suspicion of bribery, forgery, money laundering and criminal-organisation membership. Prosecutors first charged five people (18 March 2025) and then eight (early April 2025). The alleged centrepiece is a January 2021 letter signed by eight MEPs urging the Commission not to ban foreign 5G equipment. The Parliament suspended Huawei lobbyists' building access on 14 March 2025. On 16 June 2026 the Parliament lifted the immunity of one MEP, Fulvio Martusciello, and upheld the immunity of three others. Everyone named denies wrongdoing; no one has been tried or convicted.
whatIsAlleged: Belgian prosecutors ALLEGE that, under the guise of commercial lobbying and 'practised regularly and very discreetly' since 2021, Huawei representatives offered cash and 'excessive gifts' (meals, travel, and regular football-match invitations) to MEPs and assistants in exchange for favourable positions on EU 5G policy, the central artefact being a January 2021 letter. These are allegations, largely drawn from leaked investigative material; the individuals named deny them and no court has established them.
whatIsEstablished: Established as fact: Belgian federal police conducted about 21 searches on 13 March 2025, including Huawei's Brussels office. The Belgian Federal Prosecutor charged five people on 18 March 2025 and eight by early April 2025 (a charge, in Belgian law 'inculpation', is a formal investigative status, not a conviction). The European Parliament suspended Huawei lobbyists' access badges on 14 March 2025. On 16 June 2026 the Parliament lifted Fulvio Martusciello's immunity (344 for, 234 against, 25 abstentions) and upheld the immunity of Salvatore De Meo, Daniel Attard and Nikola Minchev, citing 'a flagrant scarcity of concrete elements' in the requests. The EU anti-fraud office OLAF had declined in 2022 to investigate the 2021 letter. No trial, conviction, acquittal or dismissal of the core case has been located. NO LATER PUBLIC PROCEDURAL UPDATE LOCATED AS OF 1 SEPTEMBER 2026.

title: Nathan Gill
subtitle: A former MEP, convicted of bribery for pro-Russian statements

citizen.whatHappened: Nathan Gill, a former UK Member of the European Parliament for Wales, was paid to make pro-Russian statements in the European Parliament and in the media. The payments came from Oleg Voloshyn, acting for the pro-Kremlin Ukrainian politician Viktor Medvedchuk. Gill pleaded guilty to eight counts of bribery and, on 21 November 2025, was sentenced at the Old Bailey to 10 years and 6 months in prison. The court has started proceeds-of-crime proceedings to claw back the money.

money.label: BRIBES — COURT-ESTABLISHED
money.note: The total the court found Gill accepted in cash between December 2018 and July 2019. He was convicted; proceeds-of-crime proceedings have begun.

citizen.johnLine: The speeches were written by someone else and paid for in cash. John has questions about the editing process.

whatIsAlleged: The court made clear that the case was NOT presented on the basis that the other MEPs whom Gill enlisted to give interviews knew about his financial motivation. No wrongdoing is alleged against them here.
whatIsEstablished: Established by the court (guilty plea and sentencing remarks): Gill, an MEP for Wales (2014-2020), accepted money on eight occasions between December 2018 and July 2019 to make statements favourable to Russian interests in the European Parliament and the media, using scripts supplied by Oleg Voloshyn. The court found Voloshyn to be 'the architect of these bribes' and Viktor Medvedchuk to be 'the ultimate source of the requests and the money'. Gill pleaded guilty to eight counts of bribery (section 2, Bribery Act 2010) on 26 September 2025 and was sentenced to 10 years and 6 months on 21 November 2025 at the Central Criminal Court. Proceeds-of-crime proceedings were commenced.

title: Agrofert / Andrej Babis
subtitle: An EU conflict-of-interest finding over subsidies to a prime minister's former company

citizen.whatHappened: The European Commission audited how Czech EU subsidies were handled and found that Andrej Babis, then Czech Prime Minister, had a conflict of interest: he could influence how EU money was handed out while remaining the beneficial owner of Agrofert, the large group he founded. The Commission said the affected EU money had not actually been paid out, so the EU budget was protected. A separate Czech criminal case (the 'Stork Nest' subsidy) is a different matter and has not ended in a conviction. Babis and Agrofert reject the findings.

money.label: EU FUNDING — AUDIT-QUESTIONED, BUDGET PROTECTED
money.note: The Commission said no affected expenditure had been declared, so the EU budget was 'fully protected'. This is an administrative audit finding, not a proven theft or a criminal finding.

citizen.johnLine: The conflict of interest was found, the money was not paid, and everyone disagreed about all of it.

whatIsAlleged: A separate Czech criminal case, known as 'Stork Nest', concerns an EU subsidy of about €2 million and is distinct from the Commission's conflict-of-interest audit. Babis was acquitted twice; the most recent acquittal was overturned on appeal in 2025 and proceedings continue. He denies wrongdoing and has not been convicted.
whatIsEstablished: Established (administrative audit): the European Commission's audit of Czech management and control systems (period 2014-2020) confirmed that Andrej Babis was in a conflict of interest, because as Prime Minister he could influence the allocation of EU subsidies while remaining the beneficial owner of the Agrofert group he founded. On 19 May 2021, Commissioner Johannes Hahn told the European Parliament that 'no expenditure has been declared for any of the operations affected by this audit' and that the EU budget 'has been and remains fully protected'. This is an administrative audit finding, not a criminal finding. Babis and Agrofert contest it.

money.description: Per Commissioner Hahn (19 May 2021), no expenditure was declared for the operations the audit flagged, so the EU budget was 'fully protected'. Nothing was wrongly paid out.
Amounts flagged for possible recovery were reported in the press (around €11 million) but are not stated in the primary Commission/Parliament release used here.

title: Frontex / Fabrice Leggeri
subtitle: The EU border agency, its director, and a refused budget discharge

citizen.whatHappened: OLAF, the EU's anti-fraud office, investigated the EU border agency Frontex and its director Fabrice Leggeri. After an OLAF report revealed misconduct, Leggeri resigned in April 2022. In October 2022 the European Parliament refused to sign off Frontex's 2020 accounts, citing serious misconduct, involvement in illegal 'pushbacks' of asylum seekers, and harassment problems. These are administrative and political findings, not a criminal conviction. In 2026 a French court ordered a separate judicial investigation into Leggeri; no charges have been filed.

money.label: BUDGET DISCHARGE REFUSED
money.note: The European Parliament refused to approve Frontex's 2020 budget discharge. This is a political and budgetary accountability decision, not a finding that money was stolen.

citizen.johnLine: The agency was told its 2020 paperwork would not be approved, and the director had already left the building.

whatIsAlleged: In 2026 the Paris Court of Appeal ordered a judicial investigation into Leggeri over alleged complicity in crimes against humanity linked to migrant interceptions, following a complaint by a human-rights organisation. No charges have been filed and the presumption of innocence applies.
whatIsEstablished: Established (institutional): OLAF investigated Frontex and its then-director Fabrice Leggeri and found misconduct; Leggeri resigned on 28 April 2022 following the OLAF report. On 13 October 2022 the European Parliament refused to grant Frontex's 2020 budget discharge by 345 votes to 284 with 8 abstentions, citing serious misconduct under the previous leadership, a failure to protect fundamental rights, alleged involvement in illegal pushbacks of at least 957 people between March 2020 and September 2021, and harassment problems (17 reported cases in 2020). These are administrative and political findings, not a criminal conviction of any individual.

money.description: The European Parliament refused to sign off Frontex's 2020 budget discharge. No specific sum was found to be stolen or recovered; the refusal is an accountability decision.
